contentBlocks.title: How to Apply for a SASSA Grant
contentBlocks.description: Applying for a SASSA social grant is free, and most rejections happen because of missing documents or choosing the wrong grant — not because you don't qualify. This guide walks you through choosing the right grant, gathering every document, submitting your application, and tracking it to payment.

contentBlocks.text: How to Apply for a SASSA Grant

Every year millions of South Africans apply for social grants, and a large share of applications are delayed or declined for avoidable reasons: the wrong grant was chosen, a document was missing, or the means test revealed undeclared income. This guide covers the full process for permanent grants such as the Older Persons, Disability, and Child Support grants, plus the online process for the SRD R370 grant.

This guide is for anyone applying for the first time, reapplying after a life change, or helping a family member through the process. If your application has already been declined, read our appeal guide instead.

Before collecting documents, confirm which grant actually matches your situation. Applying for the wrong grant wastes weeks — the application will be assessed against that grant's criteria and declined if they don't fit. Use this overview of the main grants and their current amounts:

rows: South Africans aged 60 and above who pass the means test
People aged 18-59 with a physical or mental disability confirmed by a state medical assessment
Primary caregivers of children under 18 who pass the means test
Court-appointed foster parents of placed children
Caregivers of children with severe disabilities requiring full-time care
Former soldiers of the Second World War or Korean War aged 60+
Grant recipients who need full-time attendant care
Unemployed adults aged 18-60 with no other income or support (applied online)
contentBlocks.caption: Main SASSA grants and current monthly amounts

contentBlocks.text: Each grant page in our Grant Library explains its exact eligibility rules. Two quick examples: you cannot receive an Older Persons Grant while earning above the income threshold, and you cannot receive the SRD R370 if you receive UIF, NSFAS funding, or any other social grant. When two grants seem possible — for example a grandmother caring for grandchildren might qualify for both Child Support (as caregiver) and Older Persons — you may apply for each separately if you meet their criteria.
The Application Process, Step by Step

steps.title: Check your eligibility in detail
steps.description: Read the specific requirements for your grant — age limits, income thresholds, residency rules, and medical criteria. Our Grant Library and eligibility pages cover each one.

steps.title: Gather all original documents
steps.description: Collect the originals plus photocopies of everything listed in the checklist below. Missing documents are the number-one cause of repeat visits and delays.

steps.title: Visit your nearest SASSA office
steps.description: Permanent grant applications must be made in person. Arrive early — queues form before opening time. No appointment is needed, but some offices run booking systems for Disability assessments.

steps.title: Complete the application with an officer
steps.description: A SASSA officer fills in the official form with you. Do not sign until you have checked that everything is correct. Your fingerprints will be taken as part of identity verification.

steps.title: Undergo screening (grant-specific)
steps.description: Disability and Care Dependency applications require a state medical assessment. The officer will book your appointment or refer you to a district surgeon. Marriage, divorce, and income checks are run against departmental databases.

steps.title: Receive your dated receipt
steps.description: You will get a receipt with a reference number. Photograph it and keep the paper copy safe — you need this number for status checks and follow-ups.

steps.title: Track your application
steps.description: Check progress via the WhatsApp line (082 046 8553), the helpline (0800 60 10 11), or your local office using your reference number. Processing takes up to three months.

steps.title: Receive the decision and first payment
steps.description: If approved, payments are backdated to your application date. If declined, you will receive written reasons and can appeal within 90 days.

items: SASSA local offices: all permanent grants (Older Persons, Disability, Child Support, Foster Care, Care Dependency). This is the only channel for these grants.
Online at srd.sassa.gov.za: the SRD R370 grant only. The whole application takes about 10 minutes and requires only your ID number, contact details, and banking information.
WhatsApp 082 046 8553: SRD R370 applications and status queries.
Home visits: if you are bedridden or too ill to travel, ask a family member to arrange a home visit through your local office.

documents.label: Your original 13-digit barcoded South African ID or smart card
documents.notes: Temporary IDs are accepted while waiting for the official document

documents.label: Proof of residence (utility bill, affidavit, or council letter)
documents.notes: If you live in an informal settlement, a confirmation letter from your ward councillor works

documents.label: Latest 3 months bank statements
documents.notes: Required if you have a bank account; shows the means test assessor your real financial position

documents.label: Marriage certificate (if married) or divorce order
documents.notes: Spousal income counts toward your means test

documents.label: UI-19 form from the Department of Labour (if previously employed)
Birth certificates of children (Child Support, Care Dependency applications)
School attendance proof (children 7-18 on Child Support Grant)
documents.notes: Needed later; the child's caregiver must confirm school enrolment annually

documents.label: Medical report / referral notes (Disability, Care Dependency)
documents.notes: The state assessment is arranged by SASSA, but bring any existing medical evidence

documents.label: Court order placing the child in your care (Foster Care)

contentBlocks.text: Most permanent grants are subject to a means test — an assessment of your income and assets to confirm you genuinely need support. Your own income and, if you are married, your spouse's income count together. Assets such as property are also considered. The thresholds change annually; our understanding-the-means-test guide breaks down the current numbers with worked examples.

contentBlocks.title: Declare Everything
contentBlocks.text: Do not hide income or bank accounts. SASSA verifies declarations against bank and employment databases, and undeclared income discovered later leads to suspension and demands to repay. Declaring income honestly may still leave you eligible.

rows: Form completed, biometrics captured, receipt issued with reference number
Identity, marital status, income, and database checks are completed
Appointment with a state doctor; results feed into the decision
Application approved or declined with written reasons
Approved grants are backdated to the application date

contentBlocks.text: You do not pay anything at any stage. If anyone asks for money to speed up an application — including so-called agents outside SASSA offices — report them to the fraud hotline on 0800 601 011.

faqs.question: Can I apply online for a SASSA grant?
faqs.answer: Only the SRD R370 grant accepts fully online applications, at srd.sassa.gov.za. All permanent grants require an in-person office visit because biometrics and original documents must be verified.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to apply?
faqs.answer: Nothing. Every SASSA service is free. Report anyone demanding payment for applications, fast-tracking, or forms to the fraud line on 0800 601 011.

faqs.question: How long does approval take?
faqs.answer: Up to three months by law. Simple applications are often decided faster; those needing medical assessments take longer. Payments are backdated to your application date regardless of how long processing took.

faqs.question: Can I apply for multiple grants at once?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you genuinely meet each grant's separate criteria — for example an Older Persons Grant and a Child Support Grant as caregiver. You cannot receive overlapping personal grants like Disability and Older Persons simultaneously.

faqs.question: What if I don't have an ID document?
faqs.answer: Apply for a temporary ID at Home Affairs first — SASSA accepts temporary IDs for applications. Home visits for immobile applicants can be arranged through your local office.

faqs.question: My application was declined. What now?
faqs.answer: Read the decline reason on your notification letter, then lodge an appeal within 90 days. Many declines are reversed when the right supporting documents are submitted.

faqs.question: Can someone apply on my behalf?
faqs.answer: Yes. A person you authorise (proxy) can apply for certain grants on your behalf with a letter of authority and both parties' IDs. For the SRD grant, applications must be done under your own ID and phone number.

faqs.question: When do I need to reapply or renew?
faqs.answer: Permanent grants continue without renewal but undergo periodic reviews. Foster Care Grants expire with each court order and must be renewed before expiry. The SRD grant is reassessed every month automatically.
